question: Which of the following is NOT related to the ‘Trinity of Carnatic Music’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Purandara Das**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Syama Shastri**, **Tyagaraja**, and **Muthuswami Dikshitar** are considered the 'Trinity of Carnatic Music'.
 
• They are renowned composers and are highly revered in the Carnatic music tradition.
 
• **Purandara Das** is not part of this trinity. Although he is a significant figure in Carnatic music, he lived earlier and is often referred to as the "father of Carnatic music."
 
• The contributions of the 'Trinity of Carnatic Music' have had a profound influence on the development and propagation of Carnatic music.
 
• Their compositions are still widely performed and form a crucial part of the Carnatic music repertoire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Syama Shastri** (1762–1827), **Tyagaraja** (1767–1847), and **Muthuswami Dikshitar** (1775–1835) were contemporaries and their works have been foundational in Carnatic music.
 
• They have composed thousands of kritis (songs) that are still sung and cherished by Carnatic musicians and enthusiasts alike.
 
• Their compositions are known for their intricate melodies, rich rhythmic patterns, and deep devotion.
 
• **Purandara Das** (1484–1564) is credited with systematizing the teaching of Carnatic music and composing thousands of devotional songs known as "Devaranamas".
